goldenPoints: MacConkey separates lactose fermenters (pink) from non-fermenters (pale) — Shigella and Salmonella stay pale
Rice-water stools + darting motility = Vibrio cholerae; grow it on TCBS, treat with fluids first
Acute hepatitis B = HBsAg plus IgM anti-HBc; anti-HBc IgG alone means the past
India ink shows Cryptococcus in HIV meningitis — a thick capsule in CSF
Falciparum on smear: multiple delicate rings, accole forms, crescent gametocytes — a medical emergency
Gas gangrene is Clostridium perfringens; fried-rice vomiting is Bacillus cereus
Thorn prick followed by nodules marching up the lymphatics = Sporothrix schenckii
Safety-pin bipolar rods in a bubo = Yersinia pestis, plague
First-week enteric fever: blood culture; the Widal comes later and lies often
Prosthetic-valve endocarditis is usually coagulase-negative staphylococci (S. epidermidis)
intro: Microbiology carries 13 questions per FMGE paper, and the previous-year stems are pure pattern recognition: a stool description, a stain, a culture medium, a vector, a serology panel. Bacteriology is the biggest block, with malaria, hepatitis B serology, HIV opportunists and fungal appearances close behind. Learn each organism by its one identifying trick — the exam always includes it.
subject: Microbiology
tagline: FMGE microbiology is organism-spotting: one stain, one medium, one vector, one classic picture per bug

topics.askedAs: method matched to the item being sterilised
topics.oneLiner: Moist heat for most things, hot air for glass and powders, hydrogen peroxide plasma for delicate scopes.
points: Autoclaving (121°C, 15 psi, 15-20 min) is the standard for media, linen and instruments — kills spores
Hot air oven sterilises glassware like petri dishes, oils and powders that steam cannot penetrate
Glutaraldehyde is a high-level disinfectant for endoscopes — it kills vegetative bacteria, fungi, viruses and (with time) spores
Hydrogen peroxide plasma sterilisation is used for heat-sensitive instruments like endoscopes and plastics
Gamma radiation sterilises disposable syringes, catheters and implants industrially
Ethylene oxide gas sterilises heat-sensitive equipment in hospitals
Pasteurisation kills vegetative pathogens in milk but not spores — it is disinfection, not sterilisation
Filtration (0.22 µm) sterilises heat-labile liquids like sera and antibiotic solutions
Tyndallisation (steaming on successive days) is the old method for spore-bearing media
topics.title: Sterilisation & Disinfection
topics.trap: A petri dish goes to the hot air oven, not the autoclave queue — glass and dry items are the oven's job.

topics.askedAs: medium matched to organism or purpose
topics.oneLiner: MacConkey sorts the lactose fermenters; LJ grows TB; chocolate agar feeds the fastidious.
points: MacConkey agar differentiates lactose fermenters (pink: E. coli) from non-lactose fermenters (pale: Salmonella, Shigella)
E. coli grows best on ordinary media like nutrient/MacConkey agar — it is not fastidious
Löwenstein-Jensen (LJ) medium is the classic solid medium for Mycobacterium tuberculosis
Chocolate agar (heated blood agar) grows Haemophilus influenzae and Neisseria species
TCBS agar is the selective medium for Vibrio cholerae (yellow colonies)
XLD and SS agar isolate Salmonella and Shigella from stool
Selenite F and tetrathionate broth are ENRICHMENT media for Salmonella/Shigella in stool
Sabouraud dextrose agar (SDA) is the routine fungal culture medium
Blood agar shows haemolysis patterns: alpha (viridans), beta (S. pyogenes), gamma (none)
topics.title: Culture Media & Stains
topics.trap: Enrichment broth (selenite F) is not a plating medium — sputum enrichment stems test whether you know broth from agar.

topics.askedAs: vignette picture matched to the gram-positive culprit
topics.oneLiner: Square-ended rods = anthrax, bull neck = diphtheria, crepitus = perfringens, fried rice = cereus.
points: Bacillus anthracis: gram-positive rods with square (truncated) ends and central spores; painless eschar with oedema; veterinarians and hide workers
Corynebacterium diphtheriae: grey pseudomembrane that bleeds on removal, bull neck; toxin ADP-ribosylates EF-2, halting protein synthesis
Clostridium perfringens: gas gangrene — crepitus, bronze skin, within a day of deep wounds; alpha toxin is a lecithinase
Staphylococcus aureus food poisoning: preformed toxin, vomiting within 1-6 hours of cream/custard food
Toxic shock syndrome: S. aureus TSST-1, tampon use, fever-hypotension-rash-desquamation
Bacillus cereus: reheated fried rice — emetic toxin, vomiting in a few hours
Streptococcus pyogenes: rheumatic fever after pharyngitis; beta-haemolytic, bacitracin sensitive
Listeria monocytogenes: meningitis in pregnancy, neonates and transplant patients — ampicillin covers it
Actinomyces: sulphur granules in cervicofacial lumpy jaw
topics.title: Gram-Positive Bacteria
topics.trap: Diphtheria's membrane bleeds when scraped; the candidal patch wipes off easily — the scrape test separates them.

topics.askedAs: stool description or CSF picture matched to organism
topics.oneLiner: Diplococci in CSF = meningococcus; darting motility = cholera; safety pin = plague.
points: Neisseria meningitidis: gram-negative diplococci in CSF, purpuric rash, Waterhouse-Friderichsen adrenal collapse
Vibrio cholerae: rice-water stools, darting (shooting-star) motility, comma shape, grows on TCBS; El Tor is the epidemic biotype
Shigella: non-motile, non-lactose fermenter — bloody dysentery with few organisms needed
Salmonella typhi: enteric fever — blood culture is the test of choice in the FIRST week; Widal rises later
Yersinia pestis: bubonic plague — painful bubo, bipolar safety-pin staining with Wayson/Giemsa
Leptospira: farmer/vet with fever and subconjunctival haemorrhage; microscopic agglutination test (MAT) confirms
Haemophilus influenzae type b: acute epiglottitis — drooling child, thumbprint sign on lateral neck X-ray
Legionella: smoker with pneumonia, confusion, diarrhoea, hyponatraemia — urinary antigen tests it; sputum Gram shows nothing
Pseudomonas: oxidase-positive, green pigment, grape-like odour, burns and ventilator pneumonia
topics.title: Gram-Negative Bacteria
topics.trap: Croup's commonest cause is parainfluenza virus; Haemophilus causes epiglottitis — similar stridor, different stem.

topics.askedAs: test or gene matched to TB and treponemes
topics.oneLiner: CBNAAT answers 'TB or not, rifampicin-resistant or not' in hours; a painless hard chancre is syphilis until disproven.
points: Ziehl-Neelsen (acid-fast) staining confirms M. tuberculosis — its mycolic acid wall resists acid-alcohol
CBNAAT/GeneXpert detects M. tuberculosis DNA AND rifampicin resistance together
Isoniazid resistance maps to katG gene mutation (shared with the pharmacology map)
Treponema pallidum: painless indurated chancre of primary syphilis; dark-ground microscopy shows it from the lesion
Yaws is caused by Treponema pallidum subspecies pertenue — skin lesions in children, non-venereal
Weil-Felix test uses Proteus OX antigens (heterophile) to diagnose rickettsial fevers like typhus
Orientia tsutsugamushi (scrub typhus) is carried by the chigger (trombiculid mite); eschar at the bite site; doxycycline treats
Brucella: undulant fever in vets and dairy workers — prolonged culture, relapsing course
Treponema cannot be grown on artificial media — like viruses, lepra bacilli and rickettsiae
topics.title: Mycobacteria, Spirochetes & Rickettsiae
topics.trap: Some organisms simply refuse artificial media: Treponema, M. leprae, rickettsiae, chlamydiae and all viruses.

topics.askedAs: serology panel interpretation, marker of infectivity
topics.oneLiner: HBsAg + IgM anti-HBc = acute; HBeAg = highly infectious; anti-HBs alone = vaccinated.
points: HBsAg positive + IgM anti-HBc positive = acute hepatitis B infection
HBeAg marks high infectivity and active replication; anti-HBe signals lower infectivity
Anti-HBs alone (no anti-HBc) = vaccine-induced immunity
Window period of hepatitis B: only IgM anti-HBc is positive
HIV enters cells through CD4 with CCR5/CXCR4 co-receptors (gp120 binding)
Tenofovir is active against both HIV and hepatitis B — the overlap drug
Hepatitis A and E spread faeco-orally; E is dangerous in pregnancy
HCV is the hepatitis most likely to become chronic and is blood-borne
Infectious state of hepatitis B is best marked by HBeAg (and HBV DNA)

head: Marker
Meaning
rows: Acute/recent infection; sole marker in window period

topics.title: Hepatitis Viruses & HIV
topics.trap: Anti-HBc IgG with no HBsAg means PAST infection — students keep calling it acute; acute needs the IgM.

topics.askedAs: vector, rash pattern or virus-disease pair
topics.oneLiner: Dengue breaks bones and leaks plasma; Zika rides Aedes; rabies fears water; HPV causes cervical cancer.
points: Dengue: Aedes aegypti, retro-orbital pain, positive tourniquet test; reinfection with another serotype risks severe dengue (antibody-dependent enhancement)
Zika virus: Aedes mosquito; fetal microcephaly is the feared outcome
Rabies: Negri bodies in hippocampal neurons; antemortem diagnosis by corneal impression/skin biopsy immunofluorescence and PCR
Parvovirus B19: slapped-cheek (fifth disease) in children; aplastic crisis in haemolytic anaemia
HPV 16/18 cause cervical cancer; HPV also drives oropharyngeal cancers
HHV-8 (Kaposi sarcoma herpesvirus) causes primary effusion lymphoma and Kaposi sarcoma
Molluscum contagiosum is a poxvirus — pearly umbilicated papules
Herpes zoster: dermatomal vesicles; Tzanck smear of HSV/VZV shows multinucleated giant cells
Measles: Koplik spots precede the rash; SSPE is the late brain complication
topics.title: Viruses: Arboviruses, Exanthems & Others
topics.trap: A Tzanck smear cannot separate HSV from VZV — both give multinucleated giant cells.

topics.askedAs: smear picture or stool finding matched to parasite
topics.oneLiner: Falciparum = many rings and crescents; amoeba eats RBCs and digs flask ulcers; Giardia fattens the stool story.
points: Plasmodium falciparum: multiple infected RBCs, accole forms, crescent gametocytes — cerebral malaria, blackwater fever
Severe falciparum malaria is treated with IV artesunate (artemisinin class is first line)
Entamoeba histolytica: quadrinucleate cysts infect; trophozoites with ingested RBCs invade — flask-shaped colonic ulcers, amoebic liver abscess
Giardia lamblia: camping/stream water, bloating, fatty diarrhoea; falling-leaf motility, pear-shaped trophozoite
Trichomonas vaginalis: frothy green discharge, strawberry cervix, motile on wet mount — treat the partner too
Cryptosporidium: chronic watery diarrhoea in HIV; acid-fast oocysts in stool
Plasmodium vivax/ovale relapse from liver hypnozoites — primaquine gives radical cure (check G6PD first)
Toxoplasma: cat faeces/undercooked meat; ring-enhancing brain lesions in HIV
topics.title: Parasitology: Protozoa & Malaria
topics.trap: Ingested RBCs inside the trophozoite separate pathogenic E. histolytica from harmless E. coli.

topics.askedAs: life-cycle clue matched to the worm
topics.oneLiner: Itchy bottom at night = Enterobius; dog plus liver cyst = hydatid; barefoot hookworm walks through skin.
points: Enterobius vermicularis: nocturnal perianal itching in children; cellotape test catches the eggs
Echinococcus granulosus: dog is definitive host; hydatid cyst in liver — never aspirate casually (anaphylaxis risk)
Wuchereria bancrofti: lymphatic filariasis, elephantiasis; nocturnal blood smear for microfilariae
Ancylostoma (hookworm) larvae penetrate skin directly; iron-deficiency anaemia follows
Taenia solium: pork tapeworm; cysticercosis from eggs (neurocysticercosis seizures)
Ascaris lumbricoides: commonest helminth; Loeffler syndrome during lung migration
Schistosoma haematobium: terminal haematuria; squamous bladder cancer association
Strongyloides can autoinfect and explode into hyperinfection under steroids
topics.title: Parasitology: Helminths
topics.trap: Hydatid cyst fluid is antigenic — spillage can kill; the exam loves pairing this cyst with 'do not aspirate'.

topics.askedAs: fungal appearance on stain matched to organism
topics.oneLiner: India ink halo = Cryptococcus; acute-angle septate = Aspergillus; broad ribbon-like = Mucor.
points: Cryptococcus neoformans: India ink shows capsulated yeast in CSF — HIV meningitis; antigen test confirms fast
Aspergillus: septate hyphae branching at acute (45°) angles on GMS stain; invasive disease in neutropenia
Mucor/Rhizopus: broad, ribbon-like, sparsely septate hyphae at right angles — rhino-cerebral disease in diabetic ketoacidosis
Candida albicans: budding yeast with pseudohyphae on KOH; grows on Sabouraud agar; germ tube positive
Pneumocystis jirovecii: crushed ping-pong ball (cup-shaped) cysts on GMS — pneumonia in HIV with low CD4
Sporothrix schenckii: thorn prick, then nodules ascending along lymphatics (rose-gardener's disease)
Malassezia furfur: spaghetti-and-meatball appearance on KOH — pityriasis versicolor
Histoplasma: small intracellular yeasts in macrophages; Ohio river valley, bird/bat droppings
Dermatophytes (Trichophyton) cause tinea; prolonged steroids convert it to tinea incognito
topics.title: Mycology
topics.trap: Angle tells the pair apart: Aspergillus branches acute and septate; Mucor branches wide and ribbon-like.

topics.askedAs: syndrome picture matched to the likeliest organism
topics.oneLiner: New murmur plus IV drug use = right-sided endocarditis; prosthetic valve = epidermidis; post-antibiotic diarrhoea = C. difficile.
points: Infective endocarditis, native valve: Streptococcus viridans (dental) and S. aureus; prosthetic valve early: S. epidermidis (coagulase-negative staph)
IV drug users: S. aureus tricuspid endocarditis — septic pulmonary emboli
Clostridioides difficile: pseudomembranous colitis after clindamycin/cephalosporins — test stool for toxin
Bacterial meningitis CSF: neutrophils, high protein, low glucose; viral: lymphocytes, normal glucose
TB/fungal meningitis CSF mimics viral cells but glucose is LOW — the discriminator
Croup (laryngotracheitis): parainfluenza virus, barking cough, steeple sign
Food poisoning timing: S. aureus 1-6 h (toxin), B. cereus fried rice (emetic), C. perfringens 8-16 h (meats)
Cat-scratch disease: Bartonella henselae
Weil disease (leptospirosis): fever, jaundice, renal failure, conjunctival suffusion after flood-water exposure
topics.title: Clinical Syndromes: Meningitis, Endocarditis, Food Poisoning
topics.trap: CSF glucose separates TB meningitis (low) from viral meningitis (normal) when both show lymphocytes.

topics.askedAs: immunoglobulin order, vaccine at birth, cell wall facts
topics.oneLiner: IgM fires first, IgG lasts longest and crosses placenta; peptidoglycan gives the wall its strength.
points: IgM is the first antibody of a primary response and the fastest to appear; IgG dominates the secondary response
IgG is the only immunoglobulin crossing the placenta
Gram-negative bacteria uniquely have an outer membrane with LPS (endotoxin) — absent in gram-positives
Peptidoglycan gives the bacterial cell wall its toughness and shape
Vaccines at birth in India: BCG, OPV (zero dose) and hepatitis B
BCG is a live attenuated vaccine (M. bovis strain); live vaccines are avoided in pregnancy and severe immunodeficiency
Killed/inactivated examples: IPV, hepatitis A, rabies; toxoid examples: tetanus and diphtheria
Endotoxin = LPS of gram-negatives (heat-stable); exotoxins are proteins, heat-labile, highly antigenic
Superantigens (TSST-1, enterotoxins) cause massive T-cell activation and cytokine storm
topics.title: Immunology Basics & Vaccines
topics.trap: Diphtheria is an EXOTOXIN disease — botulism and tetanus too; endotoxin belongs to gram-negative sepsis.
